# Ricardo Dos Santos

> Product and UX designer based in Sondrio, Italy. Works at the seam of design
> and code: design engineering, AI-assisted prototyping, and design systems for
> dense, complex software. Product Designer at OneHQ since 2022. Open to new
> work, remote or in the EU.

Contact: yo@ricardo2s.me · https://ricardo2s.me

## Who he is

Ricardo Dos Santos designs the interfaces that operations teams live inside all
day: dense tables, multi-step flows, automation canvases, reporting tools. His
work is characterised by measuring a problem before designing for it, shipping
deliberately small, and being willing to argue for the unpopular feature when
the numbers support it.

He builds as well as designs. He prototypes in HTML, CSS and TypeScript, works
with light React, and uses agentic coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, MCP) as
part of his everyday design process rather than as a novelty. This site is an
example: hand-written, no framework, no build step.

## What he does

- **Design engineering** — designs that survive contact with code, prototyped
  in the browser rather than mocked up and thrown over a wall.
- **Complex and dense UI** — enterprise CRM, insurance operations, reporting,
  automation builders. Interfaces with real density and real deadlines.
- **Design systems** — component models, naming, and the governance that keeps
  them from rotting.
- **Product research** — contextual inquiry (shadowing users at their desks),
  usability testing, comprehension testing of naming and labels, synthesis.
- **AI-assisted prototyping** — using LLM tooling to move from idea to a
  working, clickable artefact in hours.

## Selected work

All three case studies are at OneHQ, an enterprise CRM for the insurance
industry. Each is written up with the research that preceded it, the trade-offs
taken, and what was cut.

- [Workflow Automation Builder](https://ricardo2s.me/cat/onehq-workflow) (2025):
  A node-based automation builder so insurance account managers could own their
  own workflows without going through engineering. 847 automations created in
  the first 90 days; three shadow Zapier accounts decommissioned. The hard part
  was not the canvas, it was getting non-technical users past the words
  "trigger" and "conditional" — renaming "On Field Change" to "When a record is
  updated" moved comprehension from 42% to 89%.
- [Work & Communication Hub](https://ricardo2s.me/cat/onehq-comhub) (2024):
  A persistent workbar and a "Speed Work" mode for power users. Median
  time-to-send dropped from 47 seconds to 19 for power users, and context
  switches per send from 6.2 to 2.1. The design argument that landed was not
  "power users want this" but "those 12% of users drive 58% of our sends".
- [Report Builder](https://ricardo2s.me/cat/onehq-reports) (2023): Replaced a
  manual slides-and-exports process with a canvas that composes reports from
  live data, with freeze-dated snapshots and scheduled delivery. Monthly report
  prep fell from 4h 28m to 22 minutes, and the support category for "wrong
  carrier name" closed entirely.
